findings.title: Unindexed `[~]` fixture line in Task 1 cannot match the parser
findings.description:
Task 1 specifies the unindexed line as `7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.`, with no `**` around the name. `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/slicePlanParser.ts:9`) requires `\*\*([^(].*?)\*\*`, and Task 2 forbids changing anything but the checkbox class.

- **Effect:** the line stays silently dropped after the fix, so Task 5's unindexed assertions and its 7-entry / `completedSlices: 5` counts cannot pass.
- **Cause:** Task 1's success text limits the bold wrap to "the indexed form", while the slice design defines the unindexed form as `N. [~] **Name** — rationale`.
- **Fix:** write the line as `N. [~] **Feature Epsilon** — cut for scope.`

findings.title: Extending the shared fixture breaks existing tests that no task updates
findings.description:
Once the unindexed line is corrected, it takes fallback index 1 (`slicePlanParser.ts:73-77`) and sorts ahead of 101 (`slicePlanParser.ts:91`). Adding both entries to `sample-slice-plan.md` then breaks these existing assertions:

- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:10` — `toHaveLength(5)`.
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:12` and `:22` — `entries[0]` and `entries[2]` shift by one.
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:128` — "every entry `indexSource: explicit`" for this fixture.
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:166-167` — description assertions on `entries[0]` and `entries[1]`.
- `packages/core/tests/introspection/ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` — `totalSlices` `toBe(5)`.

Task 5 updates only the counts at `:44-45`. Its success check runs only `-- slicePlanParser`, so its commit lands with `ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts` red, and nothing surfaces that until Task 13.

This also contradicts the slice design's last success criterion, that `[ ]`/`[x]`/`[X]` behaviour is "proven by the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture tests continuing to pass unchanged".

**Fix:** use the sibling-fixture option the design already allows, following the precedent of `mixed-index-slice-plan.md`. Leave `sample-slice-plan.md` untouched, then drop Task 5's count-update step and its added regression test.

findings.title: Task 8's "only caller passes a full SlicePlanEntry" claim is wrong
findings.description: The only caller of `resolveEntryStatus` is `resolveEntryStatusSafe` (line 740), whose `entry` parameter is itself `Pick<SlicePlanEntry, 'index' | 'isChecked'>`. Widening only line 694 fails `tsc`, which contradicts Task 8's "builds clean". Add a sub-step to widen the `Pick` at line 736 as well, and correct the success note.

findings.title: Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change is unobservable scope creep
findings.description:
Task 9 justifies the change by saying the initializer is "the fallback used if `detectDocuments` throws". It is not. The `try` either assigns at line 122 or the `catch` at lines 125-127 sets `'degraded'`, so the initial value never reaches output.

The step has no testable effect, and the design scopes `slice.ts` to "the same one-line addition". Cut the sub-step.

findings.title: MCP tool recomputes `completedSlices` from `isChecked`, with no task covering it
findings.description:
The design assumes `completedSlices` is "computed once, in the parser". `introspection_slice_plan` recomputes it with `e.isChecked` whenever a worktree index range applies.

After Task 4, worktree-filtered MCP results still exclude `[~]` entries from the count. That leaves the criterion "`completedSlices` counts it as resolved (Decision 3)" unmet on that path. Add a sub-step to Task 4 applying the same predicate there, ideally through one shared helper so the rule lives in one place, plus one assertion in `packages/mcp-server/tests/introspectionTools.test.ts`.

findings.title: `arch-status-vs-plans` half of the ConsistencyChecker criterion has no test
findings.description:
The success criterion names both `plan-status-vs-entries` and `arch-status-vs-plans`. Task 12 covers only the first.

Task 12's "complementary case" (rule still fires when status is `in-progress`) traces to no criterion. Replace it with an `arch-status-vs-plans` no-false-positive case, modelled on the existing tests at `ConsistencyChecker.test.ts:879,912`.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, too frequent, and one is not at a green point
findings.description:
- **Format:** all six markers (lines 105, 135, 179, 197, 212, 224-225) are `- [ ] Commit:` sub-items. They should be plain `**Commit**:` lines.
- **Count:** six commits is heavy for roughly ten lines of production change. Three are enough: after Task 5, after Task 10 (covering Tasks 6-10), and after Task 12 (covering Tasks 11-12).
- **Task 13:** the conditional "if any uncommitted changes remain" commit is not a defined point. Drop it.
- **Test ordering:** Task 8's only test is Task 11, which runs after the Task 10 commit. Move Task 11 directly after Task 8 so the core wiring is tested before it is committed.

findings.title: Task file is overweight for the slice
findings.description:
Thirteen tasks cover four small production edits.

- **Merge:** Tasks 2, 3 and 4 are three edits to one function in one file, sharing one test task. Make them one task.
- **Cut:** Task 5's "explicit regression test" duplicates `slicePlanParser.test.ts:8-31`; the design says the existing tests are the proof.
- **Cut:** Task 1's "Note" checkbox is not a checkable action, and its claim that a CLAUDE.md rule requires fixture-first ordering is not what that rule says.
- **Cut:** Task 13's manual walkthrough repeats what Tasks 5, 10, 11 and 12 automate. Keep the build and full-test steps.
